title: Recap or recognition in later parts
statement: A film before a later part can recap earlier parts or only show how the place now stands: one rule bans recaps, another says recaps consolidate and reveal nothing.
detail: One version of the intro-video rules says that when a later video must make the child remember, it shows the place as it now stands and never says what happened there (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 63). The other has a later part's video recap the earlier one, since nothing in a part the child has read can spoil the next: "Recapping consolidates; it does not reveal" (line 297). The same passage adds that after the first unit, multi-part texts can begin with retrieval instead of a recap (line 297), and a produced outline for a story's second part opens with a recap (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/G3/Grade 3 markdown/01 - Fantasy Classics/01 - Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp/Video Outline - Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp Part 2.docx`, line 3).
against: The first version admits that nobody has tested recognition against recap, on a story told in parts, for a child who has forgotten the earlier one (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 62).
